headline: Majors hold above 200-days but momentum stalls; whales accumulating on exchange ramps while leverage longs crowd the boat at full funding
paragraphs: The regime is intact: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving averages, and four of five carry active golden crosses (XRP and the two altcoin laggards, DOGE and ADA, do not). That structural support matters because today the tape printed red across the board, the market cap down 3.48 percent on the session and Bitcoin down 1.6 percent, yet the 200-day lines held. Over the month, though, the picture is split: Bitcoin up 21.2 percent, Ethereum up 33.3 percent, and Solana up 37.4 percent from a month ago, while on the week all three are underwater, Bitcoin down 3.7 percent, Ethereum barely down at all, and Solana down 2.1 percent. This is a market that rallied hard into August, rolled over, and is now bouncing sideways within its longer trend, never quite confirming the month's strength and never quite abandoning it either.

Momentum is quiet and diverging from trend. Across the majors, RSI-14 sits in the 50s: Bitcoin at 52.6, Ethereum at 57.3, Solana at 54.8, XRP at 56.8, BNB at 55.6. Those are neutral to slightly warm readings, neither overbought nor oversold, which means the recent uptrend has not yet exhausted itself but is not accelerating. More telling is MACD: every single asset has MACD below its signal line, a classic sign that momentum is weakening even as price holds support. This is not a breakdown, but it is a warning that the prevailing uptrend is resting. The two worst actors, DOGE and ADA, are the clearest case: both sit below their 200-day lines and show no golden cross structure, while DOGE's RSI sits at 48.2 and ADA's at 49.7, both in sub-50 territory. These assets are not confirming the broad-market hold; they are quietly failing.

Leverage positioning reveals crowding on one side of the boat. Bitcoin funding sits at 0.81 basis points per 8 hours, equivalent to 8.9 percent annualized, well into the expensive zone, and the long-to-short ratio on OKX stands at 1.73, meaning longs outnumber shorts by 73 percent. Ethereum's ratio is even more lopsided at 1.99, while XRP hits 2.46 and DOGE reaches an extreme 4.64 longs for every short. When one side crowds this deep and pays rising funding to hold the position, price action can whip violently if that consensus breaks. SOL is the exception: it shows negative funding at minus 1.0 basis points per 8 hours (minus 10.5 percent annualized), meaning shorts are paying longs to stay short. That inversion, paired with a 2.13 long-short ratio, suggests some skepticism about SOL even as it holds its trend. Liquidations over the recent window have been heavy and one-directional: Bitcoin saw 1.15 million dollars in long liquidations against 8,500 in shorts, Ethereum 141,000 longs versus 29,500 shorts, and SOL 800,000 longs versus 6,400 shorts. The market is testing longs on every bounce.

Flows tell a more complicated story. Over the last 24 hours, whales moved 238 million dollars net onto exchanges, led by 190 million in Ethereum inflows to Coinbase and Coinbase Institutional and 77 million in Bitcoin inflows to Binance. This is the opposite of the panic picture: coins moving into regulated on-ramps during a down day, not exodus into cold wallets. Yet the five-session Bitcoin ETF picture contradicts the single-day one: net outflow of 303 million versus inflow of 160 million on the 14th. Ethereum's ETF flows are clean, consistent inflows of 318 million over five sessions with 121 million on the day alone. The stablecoin float sits at 310 billion, up just 1.36 percent on the month, which means dry powder is not materially accumulating despite the price weakness. The weekly whale flow table shows a persistent pattern: the week ending August 25th saw 1.04 billion move onto exchanges, the weeks of September 1st and 8th saw smaller flows of 70 million and 68 million respectively, and this week ending September 15th a surge back to 890 million moving onto exchanges. Whales are stepping in on dips, but they are not buying in bulk; they are accumulating through the institutional ramps.

Sentiment sits at 69 on the Fear and Greed index, labeled Greed, with a 30-day range of 31 to 74. The crowd is optimistic but not euphoric, and the range itself is wide, reflecting the chop of the last month. Today's red move does not match a sentiment collapse; if anything, the persistence of Greed while price rolls over is a mild tell that the market is slower to panic than it was to celebrate. The contradiction between leverage crowding (especially in the altcoins) and the steady whale inflow onto exchanges is worth naming: professional capital is showing conviction on dips while retail and leveraged players are positioned as if this rally will not break. That gap has closed markets before.

Watch for MACD to recross above signal line on any of the majors, which would suggest momentum is re-engaging; a breach below the 200-day on Bitcoin or Ethereum would signal regime failure; and any reversal in the week-to-week whale flow pattern, which has now turned positive four weeks in a row. The liquidation asymmetry (longs getting flushed on every attempted push) remains the tape's most active warning sign.
